subject: Clearstream pilot: cost anchors, batching/caching ops, and next steps
messages:
From: Sofia Ramos <sofia@clearstreampayments.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Intro + follow-up from today's discovery

Connor — thanks for walking us through Redwood today. Quick recap from our side and what matters most as we think about a pilot: 

Pain points we confirmed:
- High per-token cost for real-time decisions across fraud and checkout flows (spiky traffic during peak hours).
- Unpredictable tail-latency on the current managed endpoints, causing declines in conversion for a few merchant segments.
- Security/segmentation requirement: logs for AI decisions must be retained for 90 days and exported to our SIEM.

Goals for a pilot (30–60 days):
- Proof that latency can be kept <120ms p95 for the checkout path under our 500 rps peak.
- Measurable unit-cost improvement (target: >=30% reduction vs current managed API) via batching/caching or cheaper model variants.
- Evidence that logs/audit can be exported to our Splunk instance.

Budget: rough internal cap is $25k–$40k for a short pilot (we can stretch if ROI is clear).

Attachments: I uploaded our sample traffic (minute-level) and a short MVP scope doc (attached).

Next asks from Clearstream: can you sketch the cost levers you'd use (batching windows, KV/prefix caching, model quantization tradeoffs) and a rough pilot SOW? Also please confirm whether dedicated capacity is required to hit the latency target or if a hosted config with routing is viable.

— Sofia
VP Product, Clearstream Payments

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@clearstreampayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + follow-up from today's discovery

Sofia — thanks for the clear summary and the sample traffic. Great to hear the priorities. High-level recap and how we'd approach the pilot: 

Quick summary of what we heard:
- Objective: p95 <120ms on checkout path at 500 rps peak; reduce per-token cost >=30%; 90-day logs pushed to Clearstream SIEM.
- Constraint: pilot budget ~ $25k–$40k.

Proposed cost/TCO levers (sketch):
- Batching: 5–20ms batching windows for checkout (adaptive). We estimate batching alone could reduce token compute by ~18–28% depending on request size distribution.
- Prefix/KV caching: for repeated verification prompts and merchant templates, expect 10–25% token savings; immediate wins if you have stable prefixes.
- Model variants & quantization: run small-scale A/B between FP16 Llama-2-ish variant and 8-bit quantized opt variant — quantization could reduce inference $/token by ~30–40% with small latency delta on optimized kernels.
- Routing by SLO: send latency-sensitive checkout requests to a low-batch, dedicated pool; route lower-SLA analytics/notifications through high-batch, lower-cost pool.

Rough pilot SOW (summary):
- Duration: 45 days (2-week ramp, 30-day measurement).
- Scope: Checkout decision path + one fraud scoring route.
- Success metrics: p95 latency <120ms (checkout), 30%+ unit-cost reduction, logs delivered to Splunk.
- Estimated cost: hosted pilot with mixed routing: $28k (baseline) — range $22k–$36k depending on reserved bursts and model mix.

I've attached a 1-page SOW and asked Marissa below for a quick ops note on batching/caching config and what we'd need from engineering. If that matches your expectations, I'll spin up a HubSpot SOW draft and propose two slots for a pilot kickoff next week.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_pilot-sow.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia@clearstreampayments.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T08:55:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + follow-up from today's discovery

Sofia — quick technical ops note to map the levers Connor proposed to actionable config and what we need from your side: 

What we'll configure in the pilot:
- Adaptive batching policy: start with a 10ms window, measure tail; if p95 moves above target, we drop to 3–5ms for checkout route.
- KV prefix caching: ship a small set of merchant prompt prefixes (you can provide top 20 templates). Cache TTL: 12h by default during pilot.
- Quantization variants: provision two model variants: 
  * default: FP16, optimized kernels (baseline latency)
  * econ: 8-bit quantized variant for high-batch routes (saves ~35% on GPU time)
- Routing rules: checkout -> low-batch pool (guaranteed bursts), fraud/analytics -> high-batch pool.

Data and infra asks from Clearstream:
- Sample traffic (you already shared) with fields: route id, average token count, peak qps per route, and percent repeat prefixes.
- Splunk ingestion endpoint + auth mechanism for log export (we support HTTP event collector or S3 export).
- Permitted latency deviation window during ramp (suggest 20% during first 5 days).

Measurement & ROI framing we'll deliver:
- Token-level breakdown by route, cost delta vs baseline, and projected monthly run-rate at steady-state.
- Example ROI: if batching + quantization hits the midpoint of our ranges (25% batching + 35% quantization), combined could yield roughly 50% effective compute savings before caching; with realistic caching (15%) net unit-cost reduction ~55% for high-repeat routes. We'll show both per-route and blended projections.

I can stand up the config in our sandbox within 48 hours once we have the Splunk endpoint and final sample CSV.

— Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: (none)

From: Paul Ingram <paul.ingram@clearstreampayments.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T14:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Intro + follow-up from today's discovery

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Two quick notes from procurement/finance side: 

1) Budget: we can commit up to $35k without exec approval; anything above that needs a short internal go/no-go (2 business days). Your $28k baseline looks doable.
2) SLAs/Exports: we prefer S3 export to our controlled bucket (SSE-KMS). Can you confirm Redwood supports S3 export with KMS-managed keys?

Next steps from Clearstream:
- I'll share S3 write credentials to your security contact (cc'ing them next).
- Sofia to confirm two kickoff windows: Tue 10/27 10am ET or Wed 10/28 2pm ET.

Let's plan to review the SOW after you update with the pilot routing and explicit cost table per route/variant.

Paul
Head of Platform Engineering, Clearstream Payments
Attachment: Clearstream_MVP_usage_metrics.csv
